title: Deep Thoughts
description: Public-domain satirical definitions curated for an absurdist, aphoristic tone.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ABASEMENT
records.text: A decent and customary mental attitude in the presence of wealth or power. Peculiarly appropriate in an employee when addressing an employer.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ABATIS
records.text: Rubbish in front of a fort, to prevent the rubbish outside from molesting the rubbish inside.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ABDICATION
records.text: An act whereby a sovereign attests his sense of the high temperature of the throne.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ABILITY
records.text: The natural equipment to accomplish some small part of the meaner ambitions distinguishing able men from dead ones. In the last analysis ability is commonly found to consist mainly in a high degree of solemnity. Perhaps, however, this impressive quality is rightly appraised; it is no easy task to be solemn.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ABRUPT
records.text: Sudden, without ceremony, like the arrival of a cannon-shot and the departure of the soldier whose interests are most affected by it. Dr. Samuel Johnson beautifully said of another author's ideas that they were "concatenated without abruption."

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ABSCOND
records.text: To "move in a mysterious way," commonly with the property of another.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ABSENT
records.text: Peculiarly exposed to the tooth of detraction; vilifed; hopelessly in the wrong; superseded in the consideration and affection of another.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ABSENTEE
records.text: A person with an income who has had the forethought to remove himself from the sphere of exaction.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ABSOLUTE
records.text: Independent, irresponsible. An absolute monarchy is one in which the sovereign does as he pleases so long as he pleases the assassins. Not many absolute monarchies are left, most of them having been replaced by limited monarchies, where the sovereign's power for evil (and for good) is greatly curtailed, and by republics, which are governed by chance.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ABSTAINER
records.text: A weak person who yields to the temptation of denying himself a pleasure. A total abstainer is one who abstains from everything but abstention, and especially from inactivity in the affairs of others.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ABSURDITY
records.text: A statement or belief manifestly inconsistent with one's own opinion.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ACADEME
records.text: An ancient school where morality and philosophy were taught.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ACCIDENT
records.text: An inevitable occurrence due to the action of immutable natural laws.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ACCOMPLICE
records.text: One associated with another in a crime, having guilty knowledge and complicity, as an attorney who defends a criminal, knowing him guilty. This view of the attorney's position in the matter has not hitherto commanded the assent of attorneys, no one having offered them a fee for assenting.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ACCORDION
records.text: An instrument in harmony with the sentiments of an assassin.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ACCOUNTABILITY
records.text: The mother of caution.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ACCUSE
records.text: To affirm another's guilt or unworth; most commonly as a justification of ourselves for having wronged him.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ACEPHALOUS
records.text: In the surprising condition of the Crusader who absently pulled at his forelock some hours after a Saracen scimitar had, unconsciously to him, passed through his neck, as related by de Joinville.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ACHIEVEMENT
records.text: The death of endeavor and the birth of disgust.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ACKNOWLEDGE
records.text: To confess. Acknowledgement of one another's faults is the highest duty imposed by our love of truth.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ACQUAINTANCE
records.text: A person whom we know well enough to borrow from, but not well enough to lend to. A degree of friendship called slight when its object is poor or obscure, and intimate when he is rich or famous.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ACTUALLY
records.text: Perhaps; possibly.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ADAGE
records.text: Boned wisdom for weak teeth.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ADAMANT
records.text: A mineral frequently found beneath a corset. Soluble in solicitate of gold.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ADDER
records.text: A species of snake. So called from its habit of adding funeral outlays to the other expenses of living.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ADHERENT
records.text: A follower who has not yet obtained all that he expects to get.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ADMINISTRATION
records.text: An ingenious abstraction in politics, designed to receive the kicks and cuffs due to the premier or president. A man of straw, proof against bad-egging and dead-catting.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ADMIRAL
records.text: That part of a war-ship which does the talking while the figure-head does the thinking.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ADMIRATION
records.text: Our polite recognition of another's resemblance to ourselves.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ADMONITION
records.text: Gentle reproof, as with a meat-axe. Friendly warning.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ADORE
records.text: To venerate expectantly.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ADVICE
records.text: The smallest current coin.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: AFFIANCED
records.text: Fitted with an ankle-ring for the ball-and-chain.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: AFFLICTION
records.text: An acclimatizing process preparing the soul for another and bitter world.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: AGE
records.text: That period of life in which we compound for the vices that we still cherish by reviling those that we have no longer the enterprise to commit.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: AGITATOR
records.text: A statesman who shakes the fruit trees of his neighbors --to dislodge the worms.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: AIR
records.text: A nutritious substance supplied by a bountiful Providence for the fattening of the poor.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ALDERMAN
records.text: An ingenious criminal who covers his secret thieving with a pretence of open marauding.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ALLIANCE
records.text: In international politics, the union of two thieves who have their hands so deeply inserted in each other's pockets that they cannot separately plunder a third.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ALLIGATOR
records.text: The crocodile of America, superior in every detail to the crocodile of the effete monarchies of the Old World. Herodotus says the Indus is, with one exception, the only river that produces crocodiles, but they appear to have gone West and grown up with the other rivers. From the notches on his back the alligator is called a sawrian.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ALONE
records.text: In bad company.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: AMBIDEXTROUS
records.text: Able to pick with equal skill a right-hand pocket or a left.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: AMBITION
records.text: An overmastering desire to be vilified by enemies while living and made ridiculous by friends when dead.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: AMNESTY
records.text: The state's magnanimity to those offenders whom it would be too expensive to punish.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ANOINT
records.text: To grease a king or other great functionary already sufficiently slippery.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ANTIPATHY
records.text: The sentiment inspired by one's friend's friend.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: APHORISM
records.text: Predigested wisdom.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: APOLOGIZE
records.text: To lay the foundation for a future offence.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: APOSTATE
records.text: A leech who, having penetrated the shell of a turtle only to find that the creature has long been dead, deems it expedient to form a new attachment to a fresh turtle.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: APOTHECARY
records.text: The physician's accomplice, undertaker's benefactor and grave worm's provider.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: APPEAL
records.text: In law, to put the dice into the box for another throw.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: APPETITE
records.text: An instinct thoughtfully implanted by Providence as a solution to the labor question.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: APPLAUSE
records.text: The echo of a platitude.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: APRIL FOOL
records.text: The March fool with another month added to his folly.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ARCHBISHOP
records.text: An ecclesiastical dignitary one point holier than a bishop.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ARCHITECT
records.text: One who drafts a plan of your house, and plans a draft of your money.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ARDOR
records.text: The quality that distinguishes love without knowledge.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ARENA
records.text: In politics, an imaginary rat-pit in which the statesman wrestles with his record.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ARISTOCRACY
records.text: Government by the best men. (In this sense the word is obsolete; so is that kind of government.) Fellows that wear downy hats and clean shirts--guilty of education and suspected of bank accounts.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ARMOR
records.text: The kind of clothing worn by a man whose tailor is a blacksmith.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ARRAYED
records.text: Drawn up and given an orderly disposition, as a rioter hanged to a lamppost.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ARREST
records.text: Formally to detain one accused of unusualness.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ARSENIC
records.text: A kind of cosmetic greatly affected by the ladies, whom it greatly affects in turn.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ART
records.text: This word has no definition. Its origin is related as follows by the ingenious Father Gassalasca Jape, S.J.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ASPERSE
records.text: Maliciously to ascribe to another vicious actions which one has not had the temptation and opportunity to commit.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: AUCTIONEER
records.text: The man who proclaims with a hammer that he has picked a pocket with his tongue.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: AUSTRALIA
records.text: A country lying in the South Sea, whose industrial and commercial development has been unspeakably retarded by an unfortunate dispute among geographers as to whether it is a continent or an island.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: BACCHUS
records.text: A convenient deity invented by the ancients as an excuse for getting drunk.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: BACK
records.text: That part of your friend which it is your privilege to contemplate in your adversity.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: BACKBITE
records.text: To speak of a man as you find him when he can't find you.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: BAIT
records.text: A preparation that renders the hook more palatable. The best kind is beauty.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: BAPTISM
records.text: A sacred rite of such efficacy that he who finds himself in heaven without having undergone it will be unhappy forever. It is performed with water in two ways--by immersion, or plunging, and by aspersion, or sprinkling.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: BAROMETER
records.text: An ingenious instrument which indicates what kind of weather we are having.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: BARRACK
records.text: A house in which soldiers enjoy a portion of that of which it is their business to deprive others.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: BASTINADO
records.text: The act of walking on wood without exertion.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: BATH
records.text: A kind of mystic ceremony substituted for religious worship, with what spiritual efficacy has not been determined.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: BATTLE
records.text: A method of untying with the teeth of a political knot that would not yield to the tongue.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: BEFRIEND
records.text: To make an ingrate.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: BEG
records.text: To ask for something with an earnestness proportioned to the belief that it will not be given.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: BEGGAR
records.text: One who has relied on the assistance of his friends.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: BEHAVIOR
records.text: Conduct, as determined, not by principle, but by breeding. The word seems to be somewhat loosely used in Dr. Jamrach Holobom's translation of the following lines from the _Dies Irae_:

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: BELLADONNA
records.text: In Italian a beautiful lady; in English a deadly poison. A striking example of the essential identity of the two tongues.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: BENEDICTINES
records.text: An order of monks otherwise known as black friars.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: BENEFACTOR
records.text: One who makes heavy purchases of ingratitude, without, however, materially affecting the price, which is still within the means of all.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: BERENICE'S HAIR
records.text: A constellation (_Coma Berenices_) named in honor of one who sacrificed her hair to save her husband.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: BIGAMY
records.text: A mistake in taste for which the wisdom of the future will adjudge a punishment called trigamy.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: BIGOT
records.text: One who is obstinately and zealously attached to an opinion that you do not entertain.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: BILLINGSGATE
records.text: The invective of an opponent.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: BLACKGUARD
records.text: A man whose qualities, prepared for display like a box of berries in a market--the fine ones on top--have been opened on the wrong side. An inverted gentleman.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: BLANK-VERSE
records.text: Unrhymed iambic pentameters--the most difficult kind of English verse to write acceptably; a kind, therefore, much affected by those who cannot acceptably write any kind.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: BODY-SNATCHER
records.text: A robber of grave-worms. One who supplies the young physicians with that with which the old physicians have supplied the undertaker. The hyena.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: BONDSMAN
records.text: A fool who, having property of his own, undertakes to become responsible for that entrusted to another to a third.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: BORE
records.text: A person who talks when you wish him to listen.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: BOTANY
records.text: The science of vegetables--those that are not good to eat, as well as those that are. It deals largely with their flowers, which are commonly badly designed, inartistic in color, and ill-smelling.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: BOTTLE-NOSED
records.text: Having a nose created in the image of its maker.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: BOUNDARY
records.text: In political geography, an imaginary line between two nations, separating the imaginary rights of one from the imaginary rights of the other.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: BOUNTY
records.text: The liberality of one who has much, in permitting one who has nothing to get all that he can.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: BRANDY
records.text: A cordial composed of one part thunder-and-lightning, one part remorse, two parts bloody murder, one part death-hell-and-the grave and four parts clarified Satan. Dose, a headful all the time. Brandy is said by Dr. Johnson to be the drink of heroes. Only a hero will venture to drink it.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: BRUTE
records.text: See HUSBAND.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CAABA
records.text: A large stone presented by the archangel Gabriel to the patriarch Abraham, and preserved at Mecca. The patriarch had perhaps asked the archangel for bread.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CABBAGE
records.text: A familiar kitchen-garden vegetable about as large and wise as a man's head.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CALAMITY
records.text: A more than commonly plain and unmistakable reminder that the affairs of this life are not of our own ordering. Calamities are of two kinds: misfortune to ourselves, and good fortune to others.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CALLOUS
records.text: Gifted with great fortitude to bear the evils afflicting another.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CALUMNUS
records.text: A graduate of the School for Scandal.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CAMEL
records.text: A quadruped (the _Splaypes humpidorsus_) of great value to the show business. There are two kinds of camels--the camel proper and the camel improper. It is the latter that is always exhibited.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CANNIBAL
records.text: A gastronome of the old school who preserves the simple tastes and adheres to the natural diet of the pre-pork period.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CANNON
records.text: An instrument employed in the rectification of national boundaries.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CANONICALS
records.text: The motley worn by Jesters of the Court of Heaven.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CAPITAL
records.text: The seat of misgovernment. That which provides the fire, the pot, the dinner, the table and the knife and fork for the anarchist; the part of the repast that himself supplies is the disgrace before meat. _Capital Punishment_, a penalty regarding the justice and expediency of which many worthy persons--including all the assassins--entertain grave misgivings.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CARMELITE
records.text: A mendicant friar of the order of Mount Carmel.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CARNIVOROUS
records.text: Addicted to the cruelty of devouring the timorous vegetarian, his heirs and assigns.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CAT
records.text: A soft, indestructible automaton provided by nature to be kicked when things go wrong in the domestic circle.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CAVILER
records.text: A critic of our own work.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CEMETERY
records.text: An isolated suburban spot where mourners match lies, poets write at a target and stone-cutters spell for a wager. The inscriptions following will serve to illustrate the success attained in these Olympian games:

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CHILDHOOD
records.text: The period of human life intermediate between the idiocy of infancy and the folly of youth--two removes from the sin of manhood and three from the remorse of age.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CLARIONET
records.text: An instrument of torture operated by a person with cotton in his ears. There are two instruments that are worse than a clarionet--two clarionets.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CLERGYMAN
records.text: A man who undertakes the management of our spiritual affairs as a method of bettering his temporal ones.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CLIO
records.text: One of the nine Muses. Clio's function was to preside over history--which she did with great dignity, many of the prominent citizens of Athens occupying seats on the platform, the meetings being addressed by Messrs. Xenophon, Herodotus and other popular speakers.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CLOCK
records.text: A machine of great moral value to man, allaying his concern for the future by reminding him what a lot of time remains to him.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CLOSE-FISTED
records.text: Unduly desirous of keeping that which many meritorious persons wish to obtain.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: COENOBITE
records.text: A man who piously shuts himself up to meditate upon the sin of wickedness; and to keep it fresh in his mind joins a brotherhood of awful examples.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: COMFORT
records.text: A state of mind produced by contemplation of a neighbor's uneasiness.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: COMMENDATION
records.text: The tribute that we pay to achievements that resembles, but do not equal, our own.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: COMMERCE
records.text: A kind of transaction in which A plunders from B the goods of C, and for compensation B picks the pocket of D of money belonging to E.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: COMMONWEALTH
records.text: An administrative entity operated by an incalculable multitude of political parasites, logically active but fortuitously efficient.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: COMPROMISE
records.text: Such an adjustment of conflicting interests as gives each adversary the satisfaction of thinking he has got what he ought not to have, and is deprived of nothing except what was justly his due.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: COMPULSION
records.text: The eloquence of power.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CONDOLE
records.text: To show that bereavement is a smaller evil than sympathy.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CONFIDANT
records.text: One entrusted by A with the secrets of B, confided by _him_ to C.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CONGRATULATION
records.text: The civility of envy.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CONGRESS
records.text: A body of men who meet to repeal laws.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CONNOISSEUR
records.text: A specialist who knows everything about something and nothing about anything else.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CONSERVATIVE
records.text: A statesman who is enamored of existing evils, as distinguished from the Liberal, who wishes to replace them with others.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CONSOLATION
records.text: The knowledge that a better man is more unfortunate than yourself.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CONSUL
records.text: In American politics, a person who having failed to secure an office from the people is given one by the Administration on condition that he leave the country.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CONSULT
records.text: To seek another's disapproval of a course already decided on.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CONTEMPT
records.text: The feeling of a prudent man for an enemy who is too formidable safely to be opposed.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CONTROVERSY
records.text: A battle in which spittle or ink replaces the injurious cannon-ball and the inconsiderate bayonet.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CONVERSATION
records.text: A fair for the display of the minor mental commodities, each exhibitor being too intent upon the arrangement of his own wares to observe those of his neighbor.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CORONATION
records.text: The ceremony of investing a sovereign with the outward and visible signs of his divine right to be blown skyhigh with a dynamite bomb.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CORPORAL
records.text: A man who occupies the lowest rung of the military ladder.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CORPORATION
records.text: An ingenious device for obtaining individual profit without individual responsibility.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CORSAIR
records.text: A politician of the seas.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: COURT FOOL
records.text: The plaintiff.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: COWARD
records.text: One who in a perilous emergency thinks with his legs.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CRAYFISH
records.text: A small crustacean very much resembling the lobster, but less indigestible.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CREMONA
records.text: A high-priced violin made in Connecticut.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CRITIC
records.text: A person who boasts himself hard to please because nobody tries to please him.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CUNNING
records.text: The faculty that distinguishes a weak animal or person from a strong one. It brings its possessor much mental satisfaction and great material adversity. An Italian proverb says: "The furrier gets the skins of more foxes than asses."

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CURSE
records.text: Energetically to belabor with a verbal slap-stick. This is an operation which in literature, particularly in the drama, is commonly fatal to the victim. Nevertheless, the liability to a cursing is a risk that cuts but a small figure in fixing the rates of life insurance.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: CYNIC
records.text: A blackguard whose faulty vision sees things as they are, not as they ought to be. Hence the custom among the Scythians of plucking out a cynic's eyes to improve his vision.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DARING
records.text: One of the most conspicuous qualities of a man in security.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DATARY
records.text: A high ecclesiastic official of the Roman Catholic Church, whose important function is to brand the Pope's bulls with the words _Datum Romae_. He enjoys a princely revenue and the friendship of God.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DAY
records.text: A period of twenty-four hours, mostly misspent. This period is divided into two parts, the day proper and the night, or day improper--the former devoted to sins of business, the latter consecrated to the other sort. These two kinds of social activity overlap.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DEBAUCHEE
records.text: One who has so earnestly pursued pleasure that he has had the misfortune to overtake it.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DEBT
records.text: An ingenious substitute for the chain and whip of the slave-driver.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DECALOGUE
records.text: A series of commandments, ten in number--just enough to permit an intelligent selection for observance, but not enough to embarrass the choice. Following is the revised edition of the Decalogue, calculated for this meridian.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DECIDE
records.text: To succumb to the preponderance of one set of influences over another set.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DEFAME
records.text: To lie about another. To tell the truth about another.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DEFENCELESS
records.text: Unable to attack.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DEGRADATION
records.text: One of the stages of moral and social progress from private station to political preferment.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DEINOTHERIUM
records.text: An extinct pachyderm that flourished when the Pterodactyl was in fashion. The latter was a native of Ireland, its name being pronounced Terry Dactyl or Peter O'Dactyl, as the man pronouncing it may chance to have heard it spoken or seen it printed.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DEJEUNER
records.text: The breakfast of an American who has been in Paris. Variously pronounced.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DELEGATION
records.text: In American politics, an article of merchandise that comes in sets.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DELIBERATION
records.text: The act of examining one's bread to determine which side it is buttered on.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DELUGE
records.text: A notable first experiment in baptism which washed away the sins (and sinners) of the world.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DELUSION
records.text: The father of a most respectable family, comprising Enthusiasm, Affection, Self-denial, Faith, Hope, Charity and many other goodly sons and daughters.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DENTIST
records.text: A prestidigitator who, putting metal into your mouth, pulls coins out of your pocket.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DEPENDENT
records.text: Reliant upon another's generosity for the support which you are not in a position to exact from his fears.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DESTINY
records.text: A tyrant's authority for crime and fool's excuse for failure.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DIAGNOSIS
records.text: A physician's forecast of the disease by the patient's pulse and purse.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DIAPHRAGM
records.text: A muscular partition separating disorders of the chest from disorders of the bowels.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DIARY
records.text: A daily record of that part of one's life, which he can relate to himself without blushing.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DICTATOR
records.text: The chief of a nation that prefers the pestilence of despotism to the plague of anarchy.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DIE
records.text: The singular of "dice." We seldom hear the word, because there is a prohibitory proverb, "Never say die." At long intervals, however, some one says: "The die is cast," which is not true, for it is cut. The word is found in an immortal couplet by that eminent poet and domestic economist, Senator Depew:

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DIGESTION
records.text: The conversion of victuals into virtues. When the process is imperfect, vices are evolved instead--a circumstance from which that wicked writer, Dr. Jeremiah Blenn, infers that the ladies are the greater sufferers from dyspepsia.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DIPLOMACY
records.text: The patriotic art of lying for one's country.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DISABUSE
records.text: To present your neighbor with another and better error than the one which he has deemed it advantageous to embrace.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DISCRIMINATE
records.text: To note the particulars in which one person or thing is, if possible, more objectionable than another.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DISCUSSION
records.text: A method of confirming others in their errors.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DISOBEDIENCE
records.text: The silver lining to the cloud of servitude.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DISOBEY
records.text: To celebrate with an appropriate ceremony the maturity of a command.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DISSEMBLE
records.text: To put a clean shirt upon the character.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DISTANCE
records.text: The only thing that the rich are willing for the poor to call theirs, and keep.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DISTRESS
records.text: A disease incurred by exposure to the prosperity of a friend.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DIVINATION
records.text: The art of nosing out the occult. Divination is of as many kinds as there are fruit-bearing varieties of the flowering dunce and the early fool.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DRAGOON
records.text: A soldier who combines dash and steadiness in so equal measure that he makes his advances on foot and his retreats on horseback.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DRAMATIST
records.text: One who adapts plays from the French.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DUCK-BILL
records.text: Your account at your restaurant during the canvas-back season.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DUEL
records.text: A formal ceremony preliminary to the reconciliation of two enemies. Great skill is necessary to its satisfactory observance; if awkwardly performed the most unexpected and deplorable consequences sometimes ensue. A long time ago a man lost his life in a duel.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: DUTY
records.text: That which sternly impels us in the direction of profit, along the line of desire.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: EAT
records.text: To perform successively (and successfully) the functions of mastication, humectation, and deglutition.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: EAVESDROP
records.text: Secretly to overhear a catalogue of the crimes and vices of another or yourself.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ECCENTRICITY
records.text: A method of distinction so cheap that fools employ it to accentuate their incapacity.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ECONOMY
records.text: Purchasing the barrel of whiskey that you do not need for the price of the cow that you cannot afford.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: EDIBLE
records.text: Good to eat, and wholesome to digest, as a worm to a toad, a toad to a snake, a snake to a pig, a pig to a man, and a man to a worm.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: EFFECT
records.text: The second of two phenomena which always occur together in the same order. The first, called a Cause, is said to generate the other--which is no more sensible than it would be for one who has never seen a dog except in the pursuit of a rabbit to declare the rabbit the cause of a dog.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: EGOTIST
records.text: A person of low taste, more interested in himself than in me.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: EJECTION
records.text: An approved remedy for the disease of garrulity. It is also much used in cases of extreme poverty.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ELECTOR
records.text: One who enjoys the sacred privilege of voting for the man of another man's choice.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ELEGY
records.text: A composition in verse, in which, without employing any of the methods of humor, the writer aims to produce in the reader's mind the dampest kind of dejection. The most famous English example begins somewhat like this:

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ELOQUENCE
records.text: The art of orally persuading fools that white is the color that it appears to be. It includes the gift of making any color appear white.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: EMANCIPATION
records.text: A bondman's change from the tyranny of another to the despotism of himself.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: EMOTION
records.text: A prostrating disease caused by a determination of the heart to the head. It is sometimes accompanied by a copious discharge of hydrated chloride of sodium from the eyes.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ENCOMIAST
records.text: A special (but not particular) kind of liar.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: END
records.text: The position farthest removed on either hand from the Interlocutor.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ENOUGH
records.text: All there is in the world if you like it.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ENTERTAINMENT
records.text: Any kind of amusement whose inroads stop short of death by injection.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ENTHUSIASM
records.text: A distemper of youth, curable by small doses of repentance in connection with outward applications of experience. Byron, who recovered long enough to call it "entuzy-muzy," had a relapse, which carried him off--to Missolonghi.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ENVELOPE
records.text: The coffin of a document; the scabbard of a bill; the husk of a remittance; the bed-gown of a love-letter.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ENVY
records.text: Emulation adapted to the meanest capacity.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: EPAULET
records.text: An ornamented badge, serving to distinguish a military officer from the enemy--that is to say, from the officer of lower rank to whom his death would give promotion.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: EPICURE
records.text: An opponent of Epicurus, an abstemious philosopher who, holding that pleasure should be the chief aim of man, wasted no time in gratification from the senses.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: EPIGRAM
records.text: A short, sharp saying in prose or verse, frequently characterized by acidity or acerbity and sometimes by wisdom. Following are some of the more notable epigrams of the learned and ingenious Dr. Jamrach Holobom:

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: EPITAPH
records.text: An inscription on a tomb, showing that virtues acquired by death have a retroactive effect. Following is a touching example:

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ERUDITION
records.text: Dust shaken out of a book into an empty skull.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ESOTERIC
records.text: Very particularly abstruse and consummately occult. The ancient philosophies were of two kinds,--_exoteric_, those that the philosophers themselves could partly understand, and _esoteric_, those that nobody could understand. It is the latter that have most profoundly affected modern thought and found greatest acceptance in our time.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: EUCHARIST
records.text: A sacred feast of the religious sect of Theophagi. A dispute once unhappily arose among the members of this sect as to what it was that they ate. In this controversy some five hundred thousand have already been slain, and the question is still unsettled.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: EULOGY
records.text: Praise of a person who has either the advantages of wealth and power, or the consideration to be dead.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: EVANGELIST
records.text: A bearer of good tidings, particularly (in a religious sense) such as assure us of our own salvation and the damnation of our neighbors.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: EXCESS
records.text: In morals, an indulgence that enforces by appropriate penalties the law of moderation.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: EXECUTIVE
records.text: An officer of the Government, whose duty it is to enforce the wishes of the legislative power until such time as the judicial department shall be pleased to pronounce them invalid and of no effect. Following is an extract from an old book entitled, _The Lunarian Astonished_--Pfeiffer & Co., Boston, 1803:

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: EXILE
records.text: One who serves his country by residing abroad, yet is not an ambassador.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: EXPERIENCE
records.text: The wisdom that enables us to recognize as an undesirable old acquaintance the folly that we have already embraced.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: EXPOSTULATION
records.text: One of the many methods by which fools prefer to lose their friends.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: EXTINCTION
records.text: The raw material out of which theology created the future state.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: FAITH
records.text: Belief without evidence in what is told by one who speaks without knowledge, of things without parallel.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: FAMOUS
records.text: Conspicuously miserable.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: FASHION
records.text: A despot whom the wise ridicule and obey.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: FELON
records.text: A person of greater enterprise than discretion, who in embracing an opportunity has formed an unfortunate attachment.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: FIB
records.text: A lie that has not cut its teeth. An habitual liar's nearest approach to truth: the perigee of his eccentric orbit.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: FICKLENESS
records.text: The iterated satiety of an enterprising affection.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: FIDDLE
records.text: An instrument to tickle human ears by friction of a horse's tail on the entrails of a cat.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: FIDELITY
records.text: A virtue peculiar to those who are about to be betrayed.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: FINANCE
records.text: The art or science of managing revenues and resources for the best advantage of the manager. The pronunciation of this word with the i long and the accent on the first syllable is one of America's most precious discoveries and possessions.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: FLAG
records.text: A colored rag borne above troops and hoisted on forts and ships. It appears to serve the same purpose as certain signs that one sees on vacant lots in London--"Rubbish may be shot here."

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: FLESH
records.text: The Second Person of the secular Trinity.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: FLOP
records.text: Suddenly to change one's opinions and go over to another party. The most notable flop on record was that of Saul of Tarsus, who has been severely criticised as a turn-coat by some of our partisan journals.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: FOLLY
records.text: That "gift and faculty divine" whose creative and controlling energy inspires Man's mind, guides his actions and adorns his life.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: FORGETFULNESS
records.text: A gift of God bestowed upon doctors in compensation for their destitution of conscience.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: FREEBOOTER
records.text: A conqueror in a small way of business, whose annexations lack of the sanctifying merit of magnitude.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: FREEDOM
records.text: Exemption from the stress of authority in a beggarly half dozen of restraint's infinite multitude of methods. A political condition that every nation supposes itself to enjoy in virtual monopoly. Liberty. The distinction between freedom and liberty is not accurately known; naturalists have never been able to find a living specimen of either.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: FRIENDLESS
records.text: Having no favors to bestow. Destitute of fortune. Addicted to utterance of truth and common sense.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: FRIENDSHIP
records.text: A ship big enough to carry two in fair weather, but only one in foul.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: FUNERAL
records.text: A pageant whereby we attest our respect for the dead by enriching the undertaker, and strengthen our grief by an expenditure that deepens our groans and doubles our tears.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: FUTURE
records.text: That period of time in which our affairs prosper, our friends are true and our happiness is assured.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: GALLOWS
records.text: A stage for the performance of miracle plays, in which the leading actor is translated to heaven. In this country the gallows is chiefly remarkable for the number of persons who escape it.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: GENEROUS
records.text: Originally this word meant noble by birth and was rightly applied to a great multitude of persons. It now means noble by nature and is taking a bit of a rest.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: GENEALOGY
records.text: An account of one's descent from an ancestor who did not particularly care to trace his own.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: GENTEEL
records.text: Refined, after the fashion of a gent.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: GEOGRAPHER
records.text: A chap who can tell you offhand the difference between the outside of the world and the inside.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: GHOST
records.text: The outward and visible sign of an inward fear.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: GLUTTON
records.text: A person who escapes the evils of moderation by committing dyspepsia.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: GOOD
records.text: Sensible, madam, to the worth of this present writer. Alive, sir, to the advantages of letting him alone.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: GOUT
records.text: A physician's name for the rheumatism of a rich patient.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: GRACES
records.text: Three beautiful goddesses, Aglaia, Thalia and Euphrosyne, who attended upon Venus, serving without salary. They were at no expense for board and clothing, for they ate nothing to speak of and dressed according to the weather, wearing whatever breeze happened to be blowing.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: GRAMMAR
records.text: A system of pitfalls thoughtfully prepared for the feet for the self-made man, along the path by which he advances to distinction.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: GRAPESHOT
records.text: An argument which the future is preparing in answer to the demands of American Socialism.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: GRAVE
records.text: A place in which the dead are laid to await the coming of the medical student.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: GRAVITATION
records.text: The tendency of all bodies to approach one another with a strength proportioned to the quantity of matter they contain--the quantity of matter they contain being ascertained by the strength of their tendency to approach one another. This is a lovely and edifying illustration of how science, having made A the proof of B, makes B the proof of A.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: GUILLOTINE
records.text: A machine which makes a Frenchman shrug his shoulders with good reason.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: HABIT
records.text: A shackle for the free.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: HADES
records.text: The lower world; the residence of departed spirits; the place where the dead live.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: HAND
records.text: A singular instrument worn at the end of the human arm and commonly thrust into somebody's pocket.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: HAPPINESS
records.text: An agreeable sensation arising from contemplating the misery of another.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: HARANGUE
records.text: A speech by an opponent, who is known as an harangue-outang.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: HARBOR
records.text: A place where ships taking shelter from storms are exposed to the fury of the customs.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: HARMONISTS
records.text: A sect of Protestants, now extinct, who came from Europe in the beginning of the last century and were distinguished for the bitterness of their internal controversies and dissensions.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: HASH
records.text: There is no definition for this word--nobody knows what hash is.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: HATRED
records.text: A sentiment appropriate to the occasion of another's superiority.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: HEAD-MONEY
records.text: A capitation tax, or poll-tax.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: HEARSE
records.text: Death's baby-carriage.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: HEAVEN
records.text: A place where the wicked cease from troubling you with talk of their personal affairs, and the good listen with attention while you expound your own.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: HEMP
records.text: A plant from whose fibrous bark is made an article of neckwear which is frequently put on after public speaking in the open air and prevents the wearer from taking cold.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: HERMIT
records.text: A person whose vices and follies are not sociable.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: HIPPOGRIFF
records.text: An animal (now extinct) which was half horse and half griffin. The griffin was itself a compound creature, half lion and half eagle. The hippogriff was actually, therefore, a one-quarter eagle, which is two dollars and fifty cents in gold. The study of zoology is full of surprises.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: HISTORIAN
records.text: A broad-gauge gossip.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: HISTORY
records.text: An account mostly false, of events mostly unimportant, which are brought about by rulers mostly knaves, and soldiers mostly fools.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: HOMOEOPATHIST
records.text: The humorist of the medical profession.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: HOMICIDE
records.text: The slaying of one human being by another. There are four kinds of homocide: felonious, excusable, justifiable, and praiseworthy, but it makes no great difference to the person slain whether he fell by one kind or another--the classification is for advantage of the lawyers.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: HOMILETICS
records.text: The science of adapting sermons to the spiritual needs, capacities and conditions of the congregation.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: HONORABLE
records.text: Afflicted with an impediment in one's reach. In legislative bodies it is customary to mention all members as honorable; as, "the honorable gentleman is a scurvy cur."

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: HOPE
records.text: Desire and expectation rolled into one.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: HOSPITALITY
records.text: The virtue which induces us to feed and lodge certain persons who are not in need of food and lodging.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: HOUSELESS
records.text: Having paid all taxes on household goods.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: HOVEL
records.text: The fruit of a flower called the Palace.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: HUMORIST
records.text: A plague that would have softened down the hoar austerity of Pharaoh's heart and persuaded him to dismiss Israel with his best wishes, cat-quick.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: HURRICANE
records.text: An atmospheric demonstration once very common but now generally abandoned for the tornado and cyclone. The hurricane is still in popular use in the West Indies and is preferred by certain old-fashioned sea-captains. It is also used in the construction of the upper decks of steamboats, but generally speaking, the hurricane's usefulness has outlasted it.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: HURRY
records.text: The dispatch of bunglers.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: HUSBAND
records.text: One who, having dined, is charged with the care of the plate.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: HYBRID
records.text: A pooled issue.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: HYDRA
records.text: A kind of animal that the ancients catalogued under many heads.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: HYPOCHONDRIASIS
records.text: Depression of one's own spirits.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: HYPOCRITE
records.text: One who, professing virtues that he does not respect secures the advantage of seeming to be what he despises.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ICHOR
records.text: A fluid that serves the gods and goddesses in place of blood.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: IDLENESS
records.text: A model farm where the devil experiments with seeds of new sins and promotes the growth of staple vices.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: IGNORAMUS
records.text: A person unacquainted with certain kinds of knowledge familiar to yourself, and having certain other kinds that you know nothing about.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ILLUMINATI
records.text: A sect of Spanish heretics of the latter part of the sixteenth century; so called because they were light weights--_cunctationes illuminati_.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ILLUSTRIOUS
records.text: Suitably placed for the shafts of malice, envy and detraction.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: IMAGINATION
records.text: A warehouse of facts, with poet and liar in joint ownership.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: IMBECILITY
records.text: A kind of divine inspiration, or sacred fire affecting censorious critics of this dictionary.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: IMMIGRANT
records.text: An unenlightened person who thinks one country better than another.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: IMMODEST
records.text: Having a strong sense of one's own merit, coupled with a feeble conception of worth in others.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: IMPARTIAL
records.text: Unable to perceive any promise of personal advantage from espousing either side of a controversy or adopting either of two conflicting opinions.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: IMPENITENCE
records.text: A state of mind intermediate in point of time between sin and punishment.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: IMPIETY
records.text: Your irreverence toward my deity.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: IMPOSITION
records.text: The act of blessing or consecrating by the laying on of hands--a ceremony common to many ecclesiastical systems, but performed with the frankest sincerity by the sect known as Thieves.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: IMPROVIDENCE
records.text: Provision for the needs of to-day from the revenues of to-morrow.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: INCOMPATIBILITY
records.text: In matrimony a similarity of tastes, particularly the taste for domination. Incompatibility may, however, consist of a meek-eyed matron living just around the corner. It has even been known to wear a moustache.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: INCUMBENT
records.text: A person of the liveliest interest to the outcumbents.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: INDIFFERENT
records.text: Imperfectly sensible to distinctions among things.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: INDIGESTION
records.text: A disease which the patient and his friends frequently mistake for deep religious conviction and concern for the salvation of mankind. As the simple Red Man of the western wild put it, with, it must be confessed, a certain force: "Plenty well, no pray; big bellyache, heap God."

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: INEXPEDIENT
records.text: Not calculated to advance one's interests.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: INFANCY
records.text: The period of our lives when, according to Wordsworth, "Heaven lies about us." The world begins lying about us pretty soon afterward.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: INFLUENCE
records.text: In politics, a visionary _quo_ given in exchange for a substantial _quid_.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: INFRALAPSARIAN
records.text: One who ventures to believe that Adam need not have sinned unless he had a mind to--in opposition to the Supralapsarians, who hold that that luckless person's fall was decreed from the beginning. Infralapsarians are sometimes called Sublapsarians without material effect upon the importance and lucidity of their views about Adam.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: INGRATE
records.text: One who receives a benefit from another, or is otherwise an object of charity.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: INJURY
records.text: An offense next in degree of enormity to a slight.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: INJUSTICE
records.text: A burden which of all those that we load upon others and carry ourselves is lightest in the hands and heaviest upon the back.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: INSURANCE
records.text: An ingenious modern game of chance in which the player is permitted to enjoy the comfortable conviction that he is beating the man who keeps the table.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: INSURRECTION
records.text: An unsuccessful revolution. Disaffection's failure to substitute misrule for bad government.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: INTENTION
records.text: The mind's sense of the prevalence of one set of influences over another set; an effect whose cause is the imminence, immediate or remote, of the performance of an involuntary act.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: INTERPRETER
records.text: One who enables two persons of different languages to understand each other by repeating to each what it would have been to the interpreter's advantage for the other to have said.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: INTERREGNUM
records.text: The period during which a monarchical country is governed by a warm spot on the cushion of the throne. The experiment of letting the spot grow cold has commonly been attended by most unhappy results from the zeal of many worthy persons to make it warm again.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: INTIMACY
records.text: A relation into which fools are providentially drawn for their mutual destruction.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: INVENTOR
records.text: A person who makes an ingenious arrangement of wheels, levers and springs, and believes it civilization.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: IRRELIGION
records.text: The principal one of the great faiths of the world.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ITCH
records.text: The patriotism of a Scotchman.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: JEALOUS
records.text: Unduly concerned about the preservation of that which can be lost only if not worth keeping.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: JUSTICE
records.text: A commodity which is a more or less adulterated condition the State sells to the citizen as a reward for his allegiance, taxes and personal service.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: KILL
records.text: To create a vacancy without nominating a successor.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: KILT
records.text: A costume sometimes worn by Scotchmen in America and Americans in Scotland.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: KINDNESS
records.text: A brief preface to ten volumes of exaction.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: KING'S EVIL
records.text: A malady that was formerly cured by the touch of the sovereign, but has now to be treated by the physicians. Thus "the most pious Edward" of England used to lay his royal hand upon the ailing subjects and make them whole--

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: KISS
records.text: A word invented by the poets as a rhyme for "bliss." It is supposed to signify, in a general way, some kind of rite or ceremony appertaining to a good understanding; but the manner of its performance is unknown to this lexicographer.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: KLEPTOMANIAC
records.text: A rich thief.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: LABOR
records.text: One of the processes by which A acquires property for B.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: LANGUAGE
records.text: The music with which we charm the serpents guarding another's treasure.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: LAST
records.text: A shoemaker's implement, named by a frowning Providence as opportunity to the maker of puns.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: LAUREL
records.text: The _laurus_, a vegetable dedicated to Apollo, and formerly defoliated to wreathe the brows of victors and such poets as had influence at court. (_Vide supra._)

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: LAWFUL
records.text: Compatible with the will of a judge having jurisdiction.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: LAWYER
records.text: One skilled in circumvention of the law.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: LAZINESS
records.text: Unwarranted repose of manner in a person of low degree.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: LEARNING
records.text: The kind of ignorance distinguishing the studious.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: LECTURER
records.text: One with his hand in your pocket, his tongue in your ear and his faith in your patience.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: LEGACY
records.text: A gift from one who is legging it out of this vale of tears.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: LEONINE
records.text: Unlike a menagerie lion. Leonine verses are those in which a word in the middle of a line rhymes with a word at the end, as in this famous passage from Bella Peeler Silcox:

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: LIAR
records.text: A lawyer with a roving commission.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: LIBERTY
records.text: One of Imagination's most precious possessions.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: LIGHTHOUSE
records.text: A tall building on the seashore in which the government maintains a lamp and the friend of a politician.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: LINEN
records.text: "A kind of cloth the making of which, when made of hemp, entails a great waste of hemp."--Calcraft the Hangman.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: LITIGANT
records.text: A person about to give up his skin for the hope of retaining his bones.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: LITIGATION
records.text: A machine which you go into as a pig and come out of as a sausage.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: LOCK-AND-KEY
records.text: The distinguishing device of civilization and enlightenment.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: LODGER
records.text: A less popular name for the Second Person of that delectable newspaper Trinity, the Roomer, the Bedder, and the Mealer.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: LOGIC
records.text: The art of thinking and reasoning in strict accordance with the limitations and incapacities of the human misunderstanding. The basic of logic is the syllogism, consisting of a major and a minor premise and a conclusion--thus:

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: LOGOMACHY
records.text: A war in which the weapons are words and the wounds punctures in the swim-bladder of self-esteem--a kind of contest in which, the vanquished being unconscious of defeat, the victor is denied the reward of success.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: LONGANIMITY
records.text: The disposition to endure injury with meek forbearance while maturing a plan of revenge.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: LONGEVITY
records.text: Uncommon extension of the fear of death.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: LOOKING-GLASS
records.text: A vitreous plane upon which to display a fleeting show for man's disillusion given.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: LOQUACITY
records.text: A disorder which renders the sufferer unable to curb his tongue when you wish to talk.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: LOSS
records.text: Privation of that which we had, or had not. Thus, in the latter sense, it is said of a defeated candidate that he "lost his election"; and of that eminent man, the poet Gilder, that he has "lost his mind." It is in the former and more legitimate sense, that the word is used in the famous epitaph:

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: LOW-BRED
records.text: "Raised" instead of brought up.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: LUMINARY
records.text: One who throws light upon a subject; as an editor by not writing about it.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: LYRE
records.text: An ancient instrument of torture. The word is now used in a figurative sense to denote the poetic faculty, as in the following fiery lines of our great poet, Ella Wheeler Wilcox:

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MACE
records.text: A staff of office signifying authority. Its form, that of a heavy club, indicates its original purpose and use in dissuading from dissent.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MACHINATION
records.text: The method employed by one's opponents in baffling one's open and honorable efforts to do the right thing.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MAGIC
records.text: An art of converting superstition into coin. There are other arts serving the same high purpose, but the discreet lexicographer does not name them.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MAGNET
records.text: Something acted upon by magnetism.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MAGNETISM
records.text: Something acting upon a magnet.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MAGNIFICENT
records.text: Having a grandeur or splendor superior to that to which the spectator is accustomed, as the ears of an ass, to a rabbit, or the glory of a glowworm, to a maggot.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MAGPIE
records.text: A bird whose thievish disposition suggested to someone that it might be taught to talk.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MAJESTY
records.text: The state and title of a king. Regarded with a just contempt by the Most Eminent Grand Masters, Grand Chancellors, Great Incohonees and Imperial Potentates of the ancient and honorable orders of republican America.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MALTHUSIAN
records.text: Pertaining to Malthus and his doctrines. Malthus believed in artificially limiting population, but found that it could not be done by talking. One of the most practical exponents of the Malthusian idea was Herod of Judea, though all the famous soldiers have been of the same way of thinking.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MAMMON
records.text: The god of the world's leading religion. The chief temple is in the holy city of New York.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MAN
records.text: An animal so lost in rapturous contemplation of what he thinks he is as to overlook what he indubitably ought to be. His chief occupation is extermination of other animals and his own species, which, however, multiplies with such insistent rapidity as to infest the whole habitable earth and Canada.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MANES
records.text: The immortal parts of dead Greeks and Romans. They were in a state of dull discomfort until the bodies from which they had exhaled were buried and burned; and they seem not to have been particularly happy afterward.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MANICHEISM
records.text: The ancient Persian doctrine of an incessant warfare between Good and Evil. When Good gave up the fight the Persians joined the victorious Opposition.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MANNA
records.text: A food miraculously given to the Israelites in the wilderness. When it was no longer supplied to them they settled down and tilled the soil, fertilizing it, as a rule, with the bodies of the original occupants.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MARTYR
records.text: One who moves along the line of least reluctance to a desired death.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MATERIAL
records.text: Having an actual existence, as distinguished from an imaginary one. Important.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MAUSOLEUM
records.text: The final and funniest folly of the rich.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MAYONNAISE
records.text: One of the sauces which serve the French in place of a state religion.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ME
records.text: The objectionable case of I. The personal pronoun in English has three cases, the dominative, the objectionable and the oppressive. Each is all three.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MEANDER
records.text: To proceed sinuously and aimlessly. The word is the ancient name of a river about one hundred and fifty miles south of Troy, which turned and twisted in the effort to get out of hearing when the Greeks and Trojans boasted of their prowess.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MEDAL
records.text: A small metal disk given as a reward for virtues, attainments or services more or less authentic.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MEDICINE
records.text: A stone flung down the Bowery to kill a dog in Broadway.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MEEKNESS
records.text: Uncommon patience in planning a revenge that is worth while.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MEERSCHAUM
records.text: (Literally, seafoam, and by many erroneously supposed to be made of it.) A fine white clay, which for convenience in coloring it brown is made into tobacco pipes and smoked by the workmen engaged in that industry. The purpose of coloring it has not been disclosed by the manufacturers.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MENDACIOUS
records.text: Addicted to rhetoric.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MERCHANT
records.text: One engaged in a commercial pursuit. A commercial pursuit is one in which the thing pursued is a dollar.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MERCY
records.text: An attribute beloved of detected offenders.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MESMERISM
records.text: Hypnotism before it wore good clothes, kept a carriage and asked Incredulity to dinner.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: METROPOLIS
records.text: A stronghold of provincialism.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MILLENNIUM
records.text: The period of a thousand years when the lid is to be screwed down, with all reformers on the under side.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MINE
records.text: Belonging to me if I can hold or seize it.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MINISTER
records.text: An agent of a higher power with a lower responsibility. In diplomacy an officer sent into a foreign country as the visible embodiment of his sovereign's hostility. His principal qualification is a degree of plausible inveracity next below that of an ambassador.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MINOR
records.text: Less objectionable.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MIRACLE
records.text: An act or event out of the order of nature and unaccountable, as beating a normal hand of four kings and an ace with four aces and a king.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MISCREANT
records.text: A person of the highest degree of unworth. Etymologically, the word means unbeliever, and its present signification may be regarded as theology's noblest contribution to the development of our language.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MISDEMEANOR
records.text: An infraction of the law having less dignity than a felony and constituting no claim to admittance into the best criminal society.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MISERICORDE
records.text: A dagger which in mediaeval warfare was used by the foot soldier to remind an unhorsed knight that he was mortal.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MISFORTUNE
records.text: The kind of fortune that never misses.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MONEY
records.text: A blessing that is of no advantage to us excepting when we part with it. An evidence of culture and a passport to polite society. Supportable property.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MONKEY
records.text: An arboreal animal which makes itself at home in genealogical trees.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MONOSYLLABIC
records.text: Composed of words of one syllable, for literary babes who never tire of testifying their delight in the vapid compound by appropriate googoogling. The words are commonly Saxon--that is to say, words of a barbarous people destitute of ideas and incapable of any but the most elementary sentiments and emotions.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MONSIGNOR
records.text: A high ecclesiastical title, of which the Founder of our religion overlooked the advantages.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MONUMENT
records.text: A structure intended to commemorate something which either needs no commemoration or cannot be commemorated.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MORAL
records.text: Conforming to a local and mutable standard of right. Having the quality of general expediency.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MORE
records.text: The comparative degree of too much.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MOUSQUETAIRE
records.text: A long glove covering a part of the arm. Worn in New Jersey. But "mousquetaire" is a mighty poor way to spell muskeeter.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MUGWUMP
records.text: In politics one afflicted with self-respect and addicted to the vice of independence. A term of contempt.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MUMMY
records.text: An ancient Egyptian, formerly in universal use among modern civilized nations as medicine, and now engaged in supplying art with an excellent pigment. He is handy, too, in museums in gratifying the vulgar curiosity that serves to distinguish man from the lower animals.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MYRMIDON
records.text: A follower of Achilles--particularly when he didn't lead.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: MYTHOLOGY
records.text: The body of a primitive people's beliefs concerning its origin, early history, heroes, deities and so forth, as distinguished from the true accounts which it invents later.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: NECTAR
records.text: A drink served at banquets of the Olympian deities. The secret of its preparation is lost, but the modern Kentuckians believe that they come pretty near to a knowledge of its chief ingredient.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: NEIGHBOR
records.text: One whom we are commanded to love as ourselves, and who does all he knows how to make us disobedient.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: NEPOTISM
records.text: Appointing your grandmother to office for the good of the party.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: NEWTONIAN
records.text: Pertaining to a philosophy of the universe invented by Newton, who discovered that an apple will fall to the ground, but was unable to say why. His successors and disciples have advanced so far as to be able to say when.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: NIHILIST
records.text: A Russian who denies the existence of anything but Tolstoi. The leader of the school is Tolstoi.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: NIRVANA
records.text: In the Buddhist religion, a state of pleasurable annihilation awarded to the wise, particularly to those wise enough to understand it.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: NOBLEMAN
records.text: Nature's provision for wealthy American minds ambitious to incur social distinction and suffer high life.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: NOISE
records.text: A stench in the ear. Undomesticated music. The chief product and authenticating sign of civilization.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: NOMINATE
records.text: To designate for the heaviest political assessment. To put forward a suitable person to incur the mudgobbing and deadcatting of the opposition.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: NOMINEE
records.text: A modest gentleman shrinking from the distinction of private life and diligently seeking the honorable obscurity of public office.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: NON-COMBATANT
records.text: A dead Quaker.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: NONSENSE
records.text: The objections that are urged against this excellent dictionary.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: NOTORIETY
records.text: The fame of one's competitor for public honors. The kind of renown most accessible and acceptable to mediocrity. A Jacob's-ladder leading to the vaudeville stage, with angels ascending and descending.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: NOVEMBER
records.text: The eleventh twelfth of a weariness.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: OATH
records.text: In law, a solemn appeal to the Deity, made binding upon the conscience by a penalty for perjury.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: OBLIVION
records.text: The state or condition in which the wicked cease from struggling and the dreary are at rest. Fame's eternal dumping ground. Cold storage for high hopes. A place where ambitious authors meet their works without pride and their betters without envy. A dormitory without an alarm clock.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: OBSERVATORY
records.text: A place where astronomers conjecture away the guesses of their predecessors.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: OBSTINATE
records.text: Inaccessible to the truth as it is manifest in the splendor and stress of our advocacy.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: OCCASIONAL
records.text: Afflicting us with greater or less frequency. That, however, is not the sense in which the word is used in the phrase "occasional verses," which are verses written for an "occasion," such as an anniversary, a celebration or other event. True, they afflict us a little worse than other sorts of verse, but their name has no reference to irregular recurrence.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: OCEAN
records.text: A body of water occupying about two-thirds of a world made for man--who has no gills.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: OFFENSIVE
records.text: Generating disagreeable emotions or sensations, as the advance of an army against its enemy.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: OLD
