records.text: In that stage of usefulness which is not inconsistent with general inefficiency, as an _old man_. Discredited by lapse of time and offensive to the popular taste, as an _old_ book.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: OLEAGINOUS
records.text: Oily, smooth, sleek.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: OLYMPIAN
records.text: Relating to a mountain in Thessaly, once inhabited by gods, now a repository of yellowing newspapers, beer bottles and mutilated sardine cans, attesting the presence of the tourist and his appetite.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: OMEN
records.text: A sign that something will happen if nothing happens.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: OPERA
records.text: A play representing life in another world, whose inhabitants have no speech but song, no motions but gestures and no postures but attitudes. All acting is simulation, and the word _simulation_ is from _simia_, an ape; but in opera the actor takes for his model _Simia audibilis_ (or _Pithecanthropos stentor_)--the ape that howls.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: OPIATE
records.text: An unlocked door in the prison of Identity. It leads into the jail yard.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: OPPORTUNITY
records.text: A favorable occasion for grasping a disappointment.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: OPPOSE
records.text: To assist with obstructions and objections.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: OPPOSITION
records.text: In politics the party that prevents the Government from running amuck by hamstringing it.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: OPTIMIST
records.text: A proponent of the doctrine that black is white.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ORATORY
records.text: A conspiracy between speech and action to cheat the understanding. A tyranny tempered by stenography.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ORTHODOX
records.text: An ox wearing the popular religious yoke.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ORTHOGRAPHY
records.text: The science of spelling by the eye instead of the ear. Advocated with more heat than light by the outmates of every asylum for the insane. They have had to concede a few things since the time of Chaucer, but are none the less hot in defence of those to be conceded hereafter.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: OSTRICH
records.text: A large bird to which (for its sins, doubtless) nature has denied that hinder toe in which so many pious naturalists have seen a conspicuous evidence of design. The absence of a good working pair of wings is no defect, for, as has been ingeniously pointed out, the ostrich does not fly.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: OUTCOME
records.text: A particular type of disappointment. By the kind of intelligence that sees in an exception a proof of the rule the wisdom of an act is judged by the outcome, the result. This is immortal nonsense; the wisdom of an act is to be judged by the light that the doer had when he performed it.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: OUTDO
records.text: To make an enemy.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: OUT-OF-DOORS
records.text: That part of one's environment upon which no government has been able to collect taxes. Chiefly useful to inspire poets.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: OVATION
records.text: In ancient Rome, a definite, formal pageant in honor of one who had been disserviceable to the enemies of the nation. A lesser "triumph." In modern English the word is improperly used to signify any loose and spontaneous expression of popular homage to the hero of the hour and place.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: OVERWORK
records.text: A dangerous disorder affecting high public functionaries who want to go fishing.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: OWE
records.text: To have (and to hold) a debt. The word formerly signified not indebtedness, but possession; it meant "own," and in the minds of debtors there is still a good deal of confusion between assets and liabilities.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: OYSTER
records.text: A slimy, gobby shellfish which civilization gives men the hardihood to eat without removing its entrails! The shells are sometimes given to the poor.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PAIN
records.text: An uncomfortable frame of mind that may have a physical basis in something that is being done to the body, or may be purely mental, caused by the good fortune of another.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PAINTING
records.text: The art of protecting flat surfaces from the weather and exposing them to the critic.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PANDEMONIUM
records.text: Literally, the Place of All the Demons. Most of them have escaped into politics and finance, and the place is now used as a lecture hall by the Audible Reformer. When disturbed by his voice the ancient echoes clamor appropriate responses most gratifying to his pride of distinction.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PANTHEISM
records.text: The doctrine that everything is God, in contradistinction to the doctrine that God is everything.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PANTOMIME
records.text: A play in which the story is told without violence to the language. The least disagreeable form of dramatic action.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PARDON
records.text: To remit a penalty and restore to the life of crime. To add to the lure of crime the temptation of ingratitude.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PASSPORT
records.text: A document treacherously inflicted upon a citizen going abroad, exposing him as an alien and pointing him out for special reprobation and outrage.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PASTIME
records.text: A device for promoting dejection. Gentle exercise for intellectual debility.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PATIENCE
records.text: A minor form of despair, disguised as a virtue.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PATRIOT
records.text: One to whom the interests of a part seem superior to those of the whole. The dupe of statesmen and the tool of conquerors.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PATRIOTISM
records.text: Combustible rubbish ready to the torch of any one ambitious to illuminate his name.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PEACE
records.text: In international affairs, a period of cheating between two periods of fighting.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PEDESTRIAN
records.text: The variable (an audible) part of the roadway for an automobile.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PEDIGREE
records.text: The known part of the route from an arboreal ancestor with a swim bladder to an urban descendant with a cigarette.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PENITENT
records.text: Undergoing or awaiting punishment.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PERFECTION
records.text: An imaginary state of quality distinguished from the actual by an element known as excellence; an attribute of the critic.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PERIPATETIC
records.text: Walking about. Relating to the philosophy of Aristotle, who, while expounding it, moved from place to place in order to avoid his pupil's objections. A needless precaution--they knew no more of the matter than he.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PERORATION
records.text: The explosion of an oratorical rocket. It dazzles, but to an observer having the wrong kind of nose its most conspicuous peculiarity is the smell of the several kinds of powder used in preparing it.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PERSEVERANCE
records.text: A lowly virtue whereby mediocrity achieves an inglorious success.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PESSIMISM
records.text: A philosophy forced upon the convictions of the observer by the disheartening prevalence of the optimist with his scarecrow hope and his unsightly smile.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PHILANTHROPIST
records.text: A rich (and usually bald) old gentleman who has trained himself to grin while his conscience is picking his pocket.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PHILISTINE
records.text: One whose mind is the creature of its environment, following the fashion in thought, feeling and sentiment. He is sometimes learned, frequently prosperous, commonly clean and always solemn.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PHILOSOPHY
records.text: A route of many roads leading from nowhere to nothing.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PHOENIX
records.text: The classical prototype of the modern "small hot bird."

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PHONOGRAPH
records.text: An irritating toy that restores life to dead noises.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PHOTOGRAPH
records.text: A picture painted by the sun without instruction in art. It is a little better than the work of an Apache, but not quite so good as that of a Cheyenne.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PHRENOLOGY
records.text: The science of picking the pocket through the scalp. It consists in locating and exploiting the organ that one is a dupe with.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PHYSICIAN
records.text: One upon whom we set our hopes when ill and our dogs when well.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PHYSIOGNOMY
records.text: The art of determining the character of another by the resemblances and differences between his face and our own, which is the standard of excellence.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PIANO
records.text: A parlor utensil for subduing the impenitent visitor. It is operated by depressing the keys of the machine and the spirits of the audience.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PICKANINNY
records.text: The young of the _Procyanthropos_, or _Americanus dominans_. It is small, black and charged with political fatalities.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PICTURE
records.text: A representation in two dimensions of something wearisome in three.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PIE
records.text: An advance agent of the reaper whose name is Indigestion.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PIETY
records.text: Reverence for the Supreme Being, based upon His supposed resemblance to man.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PILGRIM
records.text: A traveler that is taken seriously. A Pilgrim Father was one who, leaving Europe in 1620 because not permitted to sing psalms through his nose, followed it to Massachusetts, where he could personate God according to the dictates of his conscience.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PILLORY
records.text: A mechanical device for inflicting personal distinction --prototype of the modern newspaper conducted by persons of austere virtues and blameless lives.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PIRACY
records.text: Commerce without its folly-swaddles, just as God made it.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PITIFUL
records.text: The state of an enemy or opponent after an imaginary encounter with oneself.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PITY
records.text: A failing sense of exemption, inspired by contrast.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PLAGIARISM
records.text: A literary coincidence compounded of a discreditable priority and an honorable subsequence.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PLAGIARIZE
records.text: To take the thought or style of another writer whom one has never, never read.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PLAGUE
records.text: In ancient times a general punishment of the innocent for admonition of their ruler, as in the familiar instance of Pharaoh the Immune. The plague as we of to-day have the happiness to know it is merely Nature's fortuitous manifestation of her purposeless objectionableness.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PLAN
records.text: To bother about the best method of accomplishing an accidental result.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PLATONIC
records.text: Pertaining to the philosophy of Socrates. Platonic Love is a fool's name for the affection between a disability and a frost.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PLAUDITS
records.text: Coins with which the populace pays those who tickle and devour it.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PLEASE
records.text: To lay the foundation for a superstructure of imposition.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PLEASURE
records.text: The least hateful form of dejection.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PLEBEIAN
records.text: An ancient Roman who in the blood of his country stained nothing but his hands. Distinguished from the Patrician, who was a saturated solution.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PLEBISCITE
records.text: A popular vote to ascertain the will of the sovereign.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PLENIPOTENTIARY
records.text: Having full power. A Minister Plenipotentiary is a diplomatist possessing absolute authority on condition that he never exert it.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PLEONASM
records.text: An army of words escorting a corporal of thought.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PLOW
records.text: An implement that cries aloud for hands accustomed to the pen.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PLUNDER
records.text: To take the property of another without observing the decent and customary reticences of theft. To effect a change of ownership with the candid concomitance of a brass band. To wrest the wealth of A from B and leave C lamenting a vanished opportunity.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: POETRY
records.text: A form of expression peculiar to the Land beyond the Magazines.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: POKER
records.text: A game said to be played with cards for some purpose to this lexicographer unknown.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: POLICE
records.text: An armed force for protection and participation.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: POLITENESS
records.text: The most acceptable hypocrisy.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: POLITICS
records.text: A strife of interests masquerading as a contest of principles. The conduct of public affairs for private advantage.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: POLITICIAN
records.text: An eel in the fundamental mud upon which the superstructure of organized society is reared. When he wriggles he mistakes the agitation of his tail for the trembling of the edifice. As compared with the statesman, he suffers the disadvantage of being alive.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: POLYGAMY
records.text: A house of atonement, or expiatory chapel, fitted with several stools of repentance, as distinguished from monogamy, which has but one.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PORTABLE
records.text: Exposed to a mutable ownership through vicissitudes of possession.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PORTUGUESE
records.text: A species of geese indigenous to Portugal. They are mostly without feathers and imperfectly edible, even when stuffed with garlic.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: POSITIVE
records.text: Mistaken at the top of one's voice.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: POSITIVISM
records.text: A philosophy that denies our knowledge of the Real and affirms our ignorance of the Apparent. Its longest exponent is Comte, its broadest Mill and its thickest Spencer.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: POSTERITY
records.text: An appellate court which reverses the judgment of a popular author's contemporaries, the appellant being his obscure competitor.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PRAY
records.text: To ask that the laws of the universe be annulled in behalf of a single petitioner confessedly unworthy.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PRECIPITATE
records.text: Anteprandial.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PREDICAMENT
records.text: The wage of consistency.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PREDILECTION
records.text: The preparatory stage of disillusion.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PRE-EXISTENCE
records.text: An unnoted factor in creation.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PREFERENCE
records.text: A sentiment, or frame of mind, induced by the erroneous belief that one thing is better than another.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PREHISTORIC
records.text: Belonging to an early period and a museum. Antedating the art and practice of perpetuating falsehood.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PREJUDICE
records.text: A vagrant opinion without visible means of support.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PRELATE
records.text: A church officer having a superior degree of holiness and a fat preferment. One of Heaven's aristocracy. A gentleman of God.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PREROGATIVE
records.text: A sovereign's right to do wrong.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PRESBYTERIAN
records.text: One who holds the conviction that the government authorities of the Church should be called presbyters.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PRESCRIPTION
records.text: A physician's guess at what will best prolong the situation with least harm to the patient.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PRESENT
records.text: That part of eternity dividing the domain of disappointment from the realm of hope.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PRESENTABLE
records.text: Hideously appareled after the manner of the time and place.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PRESIDE
records.text: To guide the action of a deliberative body to a desirable result. In Journalese, to perform upon a musical instrument; as, "He presided at the piccolo."

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PRESIDENCY
records.text: The greased pig in the field game of American politics.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PRESIDENT
records.text: The leading figure in a small group of men of whom--and of whom only--it is positively known that immense numbers of their countrymen did not want any of them for President.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PREVARICATOR
records.text: A liar in the caterpillar state.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PRICE
records.text: Value, plus a reasonable sum for the wear and tear of conscience in demanding it.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PRIMATE
records.text: The head of a church, especially a State church supported by involuntary contributions. The Primate of England is the Archbishop of Canterbury, an amiable old gentleman, who occupies Lambeth Palace when living and Westminster Abbey when dead. He is commonly dead.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PRISON
records.text: A place of punishments and rewards. The poet assures us that--

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PRIVATE
records.text: A military gentleman with a field-marshal's baton in his knapsack and an impediment in his hope.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PROBOSCIS
records.text: The rudimentary organ of an elephant which serves him in place of the knife-and-fork that Evolution has as yet denied him. For purposes of humor it is popularly called a trunk.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PROOF
records.text: Evidence having a shade more of plausibility than of unlikelihood. The testimony of two credible witnesses as opposed to that of only one.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PROPERTY
records.text: Any material thing, having no particular value, that may be held by A against the cupidity of B. Whatever gratifies the passion for possession in one and disappoints it in all others. The object of man's brief rapacity and long indifference.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PROPHECY
records.text: The art and practice of selling one's credibility for future delivery.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PROSPECT
records.text: An outlook, usually forbidding. An expectation, usually forbidden.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PROVIDENTIAL
records.text: Unexpectedly and conspicuously beneficial to the person so describing it.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PRUDE
records.text: A bawd hiding behind the back of her demeanor.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PUBLISH
records.text: In literary affairs, to become the fundamental element in a cone of critics.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PUSH
records.text: One of the two things mainly conducive to success, especially in politics. The other is Pull.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: PYRRHONISM
records.text: An ancient philosophy, named for its inventor. It consisted of an absolute disbelief in everything but Pyrrhonism. Its modern professors have added that.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: QUILL
records.text: An implement of torture yielded by a goose and commonly wielded by an ass. This use of the quill is now obsolete, but its modern equivalent, the steel pen, is wielded by the same everlasting Presence.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: QUIXOTIC
records.text: Absurdly chivalric, like Don Quixote. An insight into the beauty and excellence of this incomparable adjective is unhappily denied to him who has the misfortune to know that the gentleman's name is pronounced Ke-ho-tay.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: QUORUM
records.text: A sufficient number of members of a deliberative body to have their own way and their own way of having it. In the United States Senate a quorum consists of the chairman of the Committee on Finance and a messenger from the White House; in the House of Representatives, of the Speaker and the devil.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: QUOTATION
records.text: The act of repeating erroneously the words of another. The words erroneously repeated.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: QUOTIENT
records.text: A number showing how many times a sum of money belonging to one person is contained in the pocket of another--usually about as many times as it can be got there.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RACK
records.text: An argumentative implement formerly much used in persuading devotees of a false faith to embrace the living truth. As a call to the unconverted the rack never had any particular efficacy, and is now held in light popular esteem.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RANK
records.text: Relative elevation in the scale of human worth.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RANSOM
records.text: The purchase of that which neither belongs to the seller, nor can belong to the buyer. The most unprofitable of investments.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RAPACITY
records.text: Providence without industry. The thrift of power.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RAREBIT
records.text: A Welsh rabbit, in the speech of the humorless, who point out that it is not a rabbit. To whom it may be solemnly explained that the comestible known as toad-in-a-hole is really not a toad, and that _riz-de-veau a la financiere_ is not the smile of a calf prepared after the recipe of a she banker.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RASCAL
records.text: A fool considered under another aspect.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RASCALITY
records.text: Stupidity militant. The activity of a clouded intellect.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RASH
records.text: Insensible to the value of our advice.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RATIONAL
records.text: Devoid of all delusions save those of observation, experience and reflection.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RATTLESNAKE
records.text: Our prostrate brother, _Homo ventrambulans_.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RAZOR
records.text: An instrument used by the Caucasian to enhance his beauty, by the Mongolian to make a guy of himself, and by the Afro-American to affirm his worth.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: REACH
records.text: The radius of action of the human hand. The area within which it is possible (and customary) to gratify directly the propensity to provide.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RADICALISM
records.text: The conservatism of to-morrow injected into the affairs of to-day.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RADIUM
records.text: A mineral that gives off heat and stimulates the organ that a scientist is a fool with.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RAILROAD
records.text: The chief of many mechanical devices enabling us to get away from where we are to where we are no better off. For this purpose the railroad is held in highest favor by the optimist, for it permits him to make the transit with great expedition.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: REALISM
records.text: The art of depicting nature as it is seen by toads. The charm suffusing a landscape painted by a mole, or a story written by a measuring-worm.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: REALITY
records.text: The dream of a mad philosopher. That which would remain in the cupel if one should assay a phantom. The nucleus of a vacuum.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: REAR
records.text: In American military matters, that exposed part of the army that is nearest to Congress.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: REASON
records.text: To weigh probabilities in the scales of desire.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: REASON
records.text: Propensitate of prejudice.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: REASONABLE
records.text: Accessible to the infection of our own opinions. Hospitable to persuasion, dissuasion and evasion.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: REBEL
records.text: A proponent of a new misrule who has failed to establish it.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RECOLLECT
records.text: To recall with additions something not previously known.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RECONCILIATION
records.text: A suspension of hostilities. An armed truce for the purpose of digging up the dead.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RECONSIDER
records.text: To seek a justification for a decision already made.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RECOUNT
records.text: In American politics, another throw of the dice, accorded to the player against whom they are loaded.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RECREATION
records.text: A particular kind of dejection to relieve a general fatigue.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RECRUIT
records.text: A person distinguishable from a civilian by his uniform and from a soldier by his gait.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RECTOR
records.text: In the Church of England, the Third Person of the parochial Trinity, the Curate and the Vicar being the other two.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: REDEMPTION
records.text: Deliverance of sinners from the penalty of their sin, through their murder of the deity against whom they sinned. The doctrine of Redemption is the fundamental mystery of our holy religion, and whoso believeth in it shall not perish, but have everlasting life in which to try to understand it.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: REDRESS
records.text: Reparation without satisfaction.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: REDUNDANT
records.text: Superfluous; needless; _de trop_.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: REFERENDUM
records.text: A law for submission of proposed legislation to a popular vote to learn the nonsensus of public opinion.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: REFLECTION
records.text: An action of the mind whereby we obtain a clearer view of our relation to the things of yesterday and are able to avoid the perils that we shall not again encounter.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: REFORM
records.text: A thing that mostly satisfies reformers opposed to reformation.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RELIGION
records.text: A daughter of Hope and Fear, explaining to Ignorance the nature of the Unknowable.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RENOWN
records.text: A degree of distinction between notoriety and fame--a little more supportable than the one and a little more intolerable than the other. Sometimes it is conferred by an unfriendly and inconsiderate hand.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: REPARATION
records.text: Satisfaction that is made for a wrong and deducted from the satisfaction felt in committing it.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: REPENTANCE
records.text: The faithful attendant and follower of Punishment. It is usually manifest in a degree of reformation that is not inconsistent with continuity of sin.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: REPLICA
records.text: A reproduction of a work of art, by the artist that made the original. It is so called to distinguish it from a "copy," which is made by another artist. When the two are made with equal skill the replica is the more valuable, for it is supposed to be more beautiful than it looks.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: REPORTER
records.text: A writer who guesses his way to the truth and dispels it with a tempest of words.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: REPOSE
records.text: To cease from troubling.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: REPRESENTATIVE
records.text: In national politics, a member of the Lower House in this world, and without discernible hope of promotion in the next.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: REPROBATION
records.text: In theology, the state of a luckless mortal prenatally damned. The doctrine of reprobation was taught by Calvin, whose joy in it was somewhat marred by the sad sincerity of his conviction that although some are foredoomed to perdition, others are predestined to salvation.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: REQUIEM
records.text: A mass for the dead which the minor poets assure us the winds sing o'er the graves of their favorites. Sometimes, by way of providing a varied entertainment, they sing a dirge.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RESIDENT
records.text: Unable to leave.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RESIGN
records.text: To renounce an honor for an advantage. To renounce an advantage for a greater advantage.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RESOLUTE
records.text: Obstinate in a course that we approve.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RESPECTABILITY
records.text: The offspring of a _liaison_ between a bald head and a bank account.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RESPIRATOR
records.text: An apparatus fitted over the nose and mouth of an inhabitant of London, whereby to filter the visible universe in its passage to the lungs.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RESPITE
records.text: A suspension of hostilities against a sentenced assassin, to enable the Executive to determine whether the murder may not have been done by the prosecuting attorney. Any break in the continuity of a disagreeable expectation.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RESPLENDENT
records.text: Like a simple American citizen beduking himself in his lodge, or affirming his consequence in the Scheme of Things as an elemental unit of a parade.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RESPONSIBILITY
records.text: A detachable burden easily shifted to the shoulders of God, Fate, Fortune, Luck or one's neighbor. In the days of astrology it was customary to unload it upon a star.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RESTITUTION
records.text: The founding or endowing of universities and public libraries by gift or bequest.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RESTITUTOR
records.text: Benefactor; philanthropist.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RETALIATION
records.text: The natural rock upon which is reared the Temple of Law.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RETRIBUTION
records.text: A rain of fire-and-brimstone that falls alike upon the just and such of the unjust as have not procured shelter by evicting them.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: REVEILLE
records.text: A signal to sleeping soldiers to dream of battlefields no more, but get up and have their blue noses counted. In the American army it is ingeniously called "rev-e-lee," and to that pronunciation our countrymen have pledged their lives, their misfortunes and their sacred dishonor.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: REVELATION
records.text: A famous book in which St. John the Divine concealed all that he knew. The revealing is done by the commentators, who know nothing.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: REVERENCE
records.text: The spiritual attitude of a man to a god and a dog to a man.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RHADOMANCER
records.text: One who uses a divining-rod in prospecting for precious metals in the pocket of a fool.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RIBALDRY
records.text: Censorious language by another concerning oneself.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RIBROASTER
records.text: Censorious language by oneself concerning another. The word is of classical refinement, and is even said to have been used in a fable by Georgius Coadjutor, one of the most fastidious writers of the fifteenth century--commonly, indeed, regarded as the founder of the Fastidiotic School.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RICE-WATER
records.text: A mystic beverage secretly used by our most popular novelists and poets to regulate the imagination and narcotize the conscience. It is said to be rich in both obtundite and lethargine, and is brewed in a midnight fog by a fat witch of the Dismal Swamp.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RICH
records.text: Holding in trust and subject to an accounting the property of the indolent, the incompetent, the unthrifty, the envious and the luckless. That is the view that prevails in the underworld, where the Brotherhood of Man finds its most logical development and candid advocacy. To denizens of the midworld the word means good and wise.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RIME
records.text: Agreeing sounds in the terminals of verse, mostly bad. The verses themselves, as distinguished from prose, mostly dull. Usually (and wickedly) spelled "rhyme."

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RIMER
records.text: A poet regarded with indifference or disesteem.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RIOT
records.text: A popular entertainment given to the military by innocent bystanders.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RITE
records.text: A religious or semi-religious ceremony fixed by law, precept or custom, with the essential oil of sincerity carefully squeezed out of it.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RITUALISM
records.text: A Dutch Garden of God where He may walk in rectilinear freedom, keeping off the grass.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ROAD
records.text: A strip of land along which one may pass from where it is too tiresome to be to where it is futile to go.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ROBBER
records.text: A candid man of affairs. It is related of Voltaire that one night he and some traveling companion lodged at a wayside inn. The surroundings were suggestive, and after supper they agreed to tell robber stories in turn. "Once there was a Farmer-General of the Revenues." Saying nothing more, he was encouraged to continue. "That," he said, "is the story."

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ROPE
records.text: An obsolescent appliance for reminding assassins that they too are mortal. It is put about the neck and remains in place one's whole life long. It has been largely superseded by a more complex electrical device worn upon another part of the person; and this is rapidly giving place to an apparatus known as the preachment.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ROSTRUM
records.text: In Latin, the beak of a bird or the prow of a ship. In America, a place from which a candidate for office energetically expounds the wisdom, virtue and power of the rabble.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RUIN
records.text: To destroy. Specifically, to destroy a maid's belief in the virtue of maids.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RUM
records.text: Generically, fiery liquors that produce madness in total abstainers.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RUMOR
records.text: A favorite weapon of the assassins of character.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: RUSSIAN
records.text: A person with a Caucasian body and a Mongolian soul. A Tartar Emetic.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: SACERDOTALIST
records.text: One who holds the belief that a clergyman is a priest. Denial of this momentous doctrine is the hardest challenge that is now flung into the teeth of the Episcopalian church by the Neo-Dictionarians.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: SACRAMENT
records.text: A solemn religious ceremony to which several degrees of authority and significance are attached. Rome has seven sacraments, but the Protestant churches, being less prosperous, feel that they can afford only two, and these of inferior sanctity. Some of the smaller sects have no sacraments at all--for which mean economy they will indubitable be damned.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: SACRED
records.text: Dedicated to some religious purpose; having a divine character; inspiring solemn thoughts or emotions; as, the Dalai Lama of Thibet; the Moogum of M'bwango; the temple of Apes in Ceylon; the Cow in India; the Crocodile, the Cat and the Onion of ancient Egypt; the Mufti of Moosh; the hair of the dog that bit Noah, etc.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: SAFETY-CLUTCH
records.text: A mechanical device acting automatically to prevent the fall of an elevator, or cage, in case of an accident to the hoisting apparatus.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: SAINT
records.text: A dead sinner revised and edited.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: SALAMANDER
records.text: Originally a reptile inhabiting fire; later, an anthropomorphous immortal, but still a pyrophile. Salamanders are now believed to be extinct, the last one of which we have an account having been seen in Carcassonne by the Abbe Belloc, who exorcised it with a bucket of holy water.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: SARCOPHAGUS
records.text: Among the Greeks a coffin which being made of a certain kind of carnivorous stone, had the peculiar property of devouring the body placed in it. The sarcophagus known to modern obsequiographers is commonly a product of the carpenter's art.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: SATAN
records.text: One of the Creator's lamentable mistakes, repented in sashcloth and axes. Being instated as an archangel, Satan made himself multifariously objectionable and was finally expelled from Heaven. Halfway in his descent he paused, bent his head in thought a moment and at last went back. "There is one favor that I should like to ask," said he.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: SATIETY
records.text: The feeling that one has for the plate after he has eaten its contents, madam.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: SAUCE
records.text: The one infallible sign of civilization and enlightenment. A people with no sauces has one thousand vices; a people with one sauce has only nine hundred and ninety-nine. For every sauce invented and accepted a vice is renounced and forgiven.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: SAW
records.text: A trite popular saying, or proverb. (Figurative and colloquial.) So called because it makes its way into a wooden head. Following are examples of old saws fitted with new teeth.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: SCARABEE
records.text: The same as scarabaeus.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: SCEPTER
records.text: A king's staff of office, the sign and symbol of his authority. It was originally a mace with which the sovereign admonished his jester and vetoed ministerial measures by breaking the bones of their proponents.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: SCRAP-BOOK
records.text: A book that is commonly edited by a fool. Many persons of some small distinction compile scrap-books containing whatever they happen to read about themselves or employ others to collect. One of these egotists was addressed in the lines following, by Agamemnon Melancthon Peters:

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: SCRIBBLER
records.text: A professional writer whose views are antagonistic to one's own.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: SCRIPTURES
records.text: The sacred books of our holy religion, as distinguished from the false and profane writings on which all other faiths are based.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: SELF-ESTEEM
records.text: An erroneous appraisement.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: SELF-EVIDENT
records.text: Evident to one's self and to nobody else.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: SELFISH
records.text: Devoid of consideration for the selfishness of others.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: SENATE
records.text: A body of elderly gentlemen charged with high duties and misdemeanors.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: SHERIFF
records.text: In America the chief executive officer of a county, whose most characteristic duties, in some of the Western and Southern States, are the catching and hanging of rogues.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: SIREN
records.text: One of several musical prodigies famous for a vain attempt to dissuade Odysseus from a life on the ocean wave. Figuratively, any lady of splendid promise, dissembled purpose and disappointing performance.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: SLANG
records.text: The grunt of the human hog (_Pignoramus intolerabilis_) with an audible memory. The speech of one who utters with his tongue what he thinks with his ear, and feels the pride of a creator in accomplishing the feat of a parrot. A means (under Providence) of setting up as a wit without a capital of sense.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: SOPHISTRY
records.text: The controversial method of an opponent, distinguished from one's own by superior insincerity and fooling. This method is that of the later Sophists, a Grecian sect of philosophers who began by teaching wisdom, prudence, science, art and, in brief, whatever men ought to know, but lost themselves in a maze of quibbles and a fog of words.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: STORY
records.text: A narrative, commonly untrue. The truth of the stories here following has, however, not been successfully impeached.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: SUCCESS
records.text: The one unpardonable sin against one's fellows. In literature, and particularly in poetry, the elements of success are exceedingly simple, and are admirably set forth in the following lines by the reverend Father Gassalasca Jape, entitled, for some mysterious reason, "John A. Joyce."

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: SYCOPHANT
records.text: One who approaches Greatness on his belly so that he may not be commanded to turn and be kicked. He is sometimes an editor.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: SYLLOGISM
records.text: A logical formula consisting of a major and a minor assumption and an inconsequent. (See LOGIC.)

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: SYMBOLIC
records.text: Pertaining to symbols and the use and interpretation of symbols.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: TABLE D'HOTE
records.text: A caterer's thrifty concession to the universal passion for irresponsibility.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: TAKE
records.text: To acquire, frequently by force but preferably by stealth.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: TALK
records.text: To commit an indiscretion without temptation, from an impulse without purpose.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: TARIFF
records.text: A scale of taxes on imports, designed to protect the domestic producer against the greed of his consumer.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: TEDIUM
records.text: Ennui, the state or condition of one that is bored. Many fanciful derivations of the word have been affirmed, but so high an authority as Father Jape says that it comes from a very obvious source--the first words of the ancient Latin hymn _Te Deum Laudamus_. In this apparently natural derivation there is something that saddens.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: TEETOTALER
records.text: One who abstains from strong drink, sometimes totally, sometimes tolerably totally.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: TELEPHONE
records.text: An invention of the devil which abrogates some of the advantages of making a disagreeable person keep his distance.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: TELESCOPE
records.text: A device having a relation to the eye similar to that of the telephone to the ear, enabling distant objects to plague us with a multitude of needless details. Luckily it is unprovided with a bell summoning us to the sacrifice.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: TENACITY
records.text: A certain quality of the human hand in its relation to the coin of the realm. It attains its highest development in the hand of authority and is considered a serviceable equipment for a career in politics. The following illustrative lines were written of a Californian gentleman in high political preferment, who has passed to his accounting:

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: TORTOISE
records.text: A creature thoughtfully created to supply occasion for the following lines by the illustrious Ambat Delaso:

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: TRICHINOSIS
records.text: The pig's reply to proponents of porcophagy.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: TROGLODYTE
records.text: Specifically, a cave-dweller of the paleolithic period, after the Tree and before the Flat. A famous community of troglodytes dwelt with David in the Cave of Adullam. The colony consisted of "every one that was in distress, and every one that was in debt, and every one that was discontented"--in brief, all the Socialists of Judah.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: TRUTH
records.text: An ingenious compound of desirability and appearance. Discovery of truth is the sole purpose of philosophy, which is the most ancient occupation of the human mind and has a fair prospect of existing with increasing activity to the end of time.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: TRUTHFUL
records.text: Dumb and illiterate.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: TURKEY
records.text: A large bird whose flesh when eaten on certain religious anniversaries has the peculiar property of attesting piety and gratitude. Incidentally, it is pretty good eating.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: TWICE
records.text: Once too often.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: TYPE
records.text: Pestilent bits of metal suspected of destroying civilization and enlightenment, despite their obvious agency in this incomparable dictionary.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ULTIMATUM
records.text: In diplomacy, a last demand before resorting to concessions.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: UNDERSTANDING
records.text: A cerebral secretion that enables one having it to know a house from a horse by the roof on the house. Its nature and laws have been exhaustively expounded by Locke, who rode a house, and Kant, who lived in a horse.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: UNITARIAN
records.text: One who denies the divinity of a Trinitarian.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: UNIVERSALIST
records.text: One who forgoes the advantage of a Hell for persons of another faith.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: URBANITY
records.text: The kind of civility that urban observers ascribe to dwellers in all cities but New York. Its commonest expression is heard in the words, "I beg your pardon," and it is not inconsistent with disregard of the rights of others.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: USAGE
records.text: The First Person of the literary Trinity, the Second and Third being Custom and Conventionality. Imbued with a decent reverence for this Holy Triad an industrious writer may hope to produce books that will live as long as the fashion.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: VALOR
records.text: A soldierly compound of vanity, duty and the gambler's hope.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: VANITY
records.text: The tribute of a fool to the worth of the nearest ass.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: VIRTUES
records.text: Certain abstentions.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: VITUPERATION
records.text: Satire, as understood by dunces and all such as suffer from an impediment in their wit.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: VOTE
records.text: The instrument and symbol of a freeman's power to make a fool of himself and a wreck of his country.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: WALL STREET
records.text: A symbol of sin for every devil to rebuke. That Wall Street is a den of thieves is a belief that serves every unsuccessful thief in place of a hope in Heaven. Even the great and good Andrew Carnegie has made his profession of faith in the matter.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: WEDDING
records.text: A ceremony at which two persons undertake to become one, one undertakes to become nothing, and nothing undertakes to become supportable.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: WEREWOLF
records.text: A wolf that was once, or is sometimes, a man. All werewolves are of evil disposition, having assumed a bestial form to gratify a beastial appetite, but some, transformed by sorcery, are as humane as is consistent with an acquired taste for human flesh.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: WHANGDEPOOTENAWAH
records.text: In the Ojibwa tongue, disaster; an unexpected affliction that strikes hard.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: WHEAT
records.text: A cereal from which a tolerably good whisky can with some difficulty be made, and which is used also for bread. The French are said to eat more bread _per capita_ of population than any other people, which is natural, for only they know how to make the stuff palatable.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: WIT
records.text: The salt with which the American humorist spoils his intellectual cookery by leaving it out.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: WITTICISM
records.text: A sharp and clever remark, usually quoted, and seldom noted; what the Philistine is pleased to call a "joke."

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: WORSHIP
records.text: Homo Creator's testimony to the sound construction and fine finish of Deus Creatus. A popular form of abjection, having an element of pride.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: YANKEE
records.text: In Europe, an American. In the Northern States of our Union, a New Englander. In the Southern States the word is unknown. (See DAMNYANK.)

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: YEAR
records.text: A period of three hundred and sixty-five disappointments.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: YESTERDAY
records.text: The infancy of youth, the youth of manhood, the entire past of age.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: YOKE
records.text: An implement, madam, to whose Latin name, _jugum_, we owe one of the most illuminating words in our language--a word that defines the matrimonial situation with precision, point and poignancy. A thousand apologies for withholding it.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: YOUTH
records.text: The Period of Possibility, when Archimedes finds a fulcrum, Cassandra has a following and seven cities compete for the honor of endowing a living Homer.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ZEAL
records.text: A certain nervous disorder afflicting the young and inexperienced. A passion that goeth before a sprawl.

records.creator: Ambrose Bierce
records.title: ZIGZAG
records.text: To move forward uncertainly, from side to side, as one carrying the white man's burden. (From _zed_, _z_, and _jag_, an Icelandic word of unknown meaning.)
